message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study compares cytokine, chemokine, and MMP profiles in dogs with OA to healthy dogs and calculates sensitivities and specificities of potential biomarkers, which is a quantitative measure of agreement between animal model findings and potential human clinical utility.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "The cytokine, chemokine, and matrix metalloprotease (MMP) profiles of synovial fluid, serum, and urine from dogs with surgically induced and naturally occurring OA were compared with dogs without OA",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "musculoskeletal"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Osteoarthritis (OA) is a disease that commonly affects human and veterinary patients.",
  "model_type": "surgical",
  "model_evidence": "dogs with surgically induced and naturally occurring OA",
  "species": [
    "dog"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The dog is a nearly ideal species for translational investigation of human OA biomarkers.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Markers that exhibited significant differences between groups were identified (monocyte chemoattractant protein 1 [MCP1], interleukin 8 [IL8], keratinocyte-derived chemoattractant [KC], and MMP2 and MMP3), and their sensitivities and specificities were calculated"
}
